newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MOF to reduce treasury role of banks.
newsitem.headline: Russian MOF to reduce treasury role of banks.

text.p: The Russian government plans to limit private banks' role in servicing payments in and out of the federal budget, official sources said on Wednesday.
A source in First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin's office said the federal treasury, which is being set up, will eventually completely handle standard budgetary payments.
But banks authorised to handle payments for the government would continue to do so for special programmes, the source said.

Servicing government transfers can be extremely lucrative for Russian banks, but some have been criticised for delaying or even misappropriating government funds, exacerbating Russia's financial non-payments problem.

A senior aide to President Boris Yeltsin said in a newspaper interview published on Tuesday that Yeltsin would announce the abolition of the authorised bank system in his annual address to parliament on March 6.

"It was clear right from the beginning that the system of authorised banks was a temporary measure arising from the underdeveloped nature of the state financial system," Georgy Saratov told Moskovsky Komsomolets.
But the source in the office of Potanin, the senior cabinet minister responsible for economic policy, said the new treasury would not be able to handle payments on all programmes.
The government would continue to designate banks to handle these payments, the source said.
All together there are currently 54 authorised banks, divided into three groups.

The first group of 16, whose members must have shareholders funds of over one trillion roubles ($176.2 million) and which includes most of Russia's top banks, can handle state domestic currency and foreign debt, including Eurobonds, exports of precious metals and credits of international financial organisations.
The second group, handling payments into and out of the federal budget, includes 10 banks. The third group, handling certain state programmes, consists of 28 banks.
